title: Relay settings
goal: Point the relay at the right mail host, keep its token replaceable but never readable, and prove the setup works — then leave.
primaryQuestion: Is the relay set up to send?
_why: Configuration read rarely and changed deliberately — the settings archetype exactly. NOT a wizard, though the brief smells like setup: any knob changes alone, in any order, months apart; a wizard walks once and adds clicks forever after. The moment this screen grows a member list or per-recipient rows, that part is a collection and leaves for a list screen.

zones.name: header
zones.purpose: The template's header inside the narrow column: the screen's name and Save. Saving returns the operator to where they came from — settings are a detour, not a destination.

zones.name: check
zones.answers: Is the relay set up to send?
zones.purpose: The connection test FIRST, before any knob: it answers the screen's question directly, and most visits are 'is it working', not 'change something'. The result names what failed and the action that fixes it.

zones.name: sections
zones.purpose: Grouped rows of explained knobs — delivery (host, sender), the secret (token: write-only, paste to replace, a Badge says configured, the value never renders), and cadence (digest frequency, quiet hours). Every row's description says what changing it affects, because the operator finds things by scanning labels.

states.empty: Not a list — an unconfigured relay is the sections with empty controls and no configured Badge anywhere, plus the connection test saying what is missing. That is a settings screen's honest empty state.
states.error: A failed save keeps the Button out of its loading state with the reason beside the control that caused it; the test's result region names the failure and its fix, with the Badge carrying the verdict.

acceptance: Every row's description says what changing it affects — no control stands unexplained.
The token is never echoed: its field is empty on open, and a configured token shows as a Badge, not a value.
The connection test result names the failing piece and the action that fixes it, in words.
Any knob changes alone: no step order, no gating between sections.

behaviours.given: a relay with a saved API token
behaviours.then: the token field is empty with a configured Badge beside it; typing replaces, nothing reads back
behaviours.why: A secret a screen can display is a secret a screenshot leaks.
behaviours.pendingReason: Delivered as a single screen file ahead of the product's own repo and test harness; the test lands with the first vitest setup, named relay-settings#token-is-write-only.

data: current settings: host, sender, digest frequency, quietHours as values; the token as a BOOLEAN (configured or not) — the value never crosses to the screen
the connection test result: ok, or the named failure with its fix — inline mock state so the button really flips it
